name: Amika

modes.label: On-demand
modes.note: Hosted sandboxes bill per second at the published rates after the $50 starting credit; the homepage still offers hosted cloud devboxes as early access via a waitlist, so rates may change.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Up to 3 active users; up to 10 concurrent service-account sandboxes (sandboxes people start are never counted). $50 of credits per organization to start (see free). Past 3 active users the org moves to Team.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $30/mo per active user (anyone who starts a sandbox or sends an agent instructions that month). 10 concurrent service-account sandboxes included, then $2/mo each, prorated by the day.

plans.name: Team (20 concurrent)
plans.note: Team with 10 extra concurrent service-account sandboxes at $2/mo each ($30 + $20). The rule is linear; these steps approximate it until the engine can price a per-slot fee (a peak between steps is billed at the next step here). Source: https://www.amika.dev/pricing (2026-10-14).

plans.name: Team (50 concurrent)
plans.note: Team with 40 extra concurrent service-account sandboxes at $2/mo each ($30 + $80). The rule is linear; these steps approximate it until the engine can price a per-slot fee (a peak between steps is billed at the next step here). Source: https://www.amika.dev/pricing (2026-10-14).

plans.name: Team (100 concurrent)
plans.note: Team with 90 extra concurrent service-account sandboxes at $2/mo each ($30 + $180). The rule is linear; these steps approximate it until the engine can price a per-slot fee (a peak between steps is billed at the next step here). Source: https://www.amika.dev/pricing (2026-10-14).

plans.name: Team (300 concurrent)
plans.note: Team with 290 extra concurrent service-account sandboxes at $2/mo each ($30 + $580). The rule is linear; these steps approximate it until the engine can price a per-slot fee (a peak between steps is billed at the next step here). Source: https://www.amika.dev/pricing (2026-10-14).

plans.name: Team (1,000 concurrent)
plans.note: Team with 990 extra concurrent service-account sandboxes at $2/mo each ($30 + $1980). The rule is linear; these steps approximate it until the engine can price a per-slot fee (a peak between steps is billed at the next step here). Source: https://www.amika.dev/pricing (2026-10-14).

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom. Committed volume pricing with discounts on hosted compute and service-account sandboxes; SSO, SCIM, audit logs; GPUs and custom sandbox sizes; uptime SLA.

free.conditions: "$50 of credits per organization to start" on Free and Team; hosted sandboxes bill after it.

caveats: BYO LLM keys; no token markup. Allocated-vs-utilized CPU wording not specified: conservatively model allocated.

Plans (amika.dev/pricing, 2026-10-14): Free $0 (up to 3 active users, up to 10 concurrent service-account sandboxes); Team $30/mo per active user (10 concurrent service-account sandboxes included, then $2/mo each, prorated by the day); Enterprise custom. The old Developer $30 and Team $100 plans and per-plan monthly credits are gone; both plans get a one-time "$50 of credits per organization to start".

Only service-account sandboxes (started by an API key not tied to a person) count toward concurrency: "Sandboxes people start are never counted", and paused/stopped ones do not count. The card applies the 10-slot cap and $2/slot fee to the whole fleet, which fits API-driven agent fleets; sandboxes started by people are capped by neither. The $2/slot rule is linear; the card approximates it with Team steps at 20/50/100/300/1,000 concurrent.
Free allows at most 3 active users ("Past that, the org moves to Team and every active user is $30"); the engine has no per-plan seat cap, so a 4+ person team may be shown on Free.

Sandboxes on your own machines (Mac Mini, EC2 in your VPC, Kubernetes) run on every plan and "their hours are never charged"; the card prices only Amika-hosted sandboxes. Hosted devboxes are still offered as early access via a waitlist on the homepage while the pricing page publishes rates, so the hosted mode is flagged beta.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Storage $0.00216/GiB-h ($0.0000006/GiB-s, consistent; = $1.5768/GiB-month) per amika.dev/pricing; whether stopped sandboxes keep paying storage is unstated. Pricing example: "2 vCPU, 4 GiB of memory, and 20 GiB of storage costs about $0.37 per hour".

Docs 2026-09-28: SSH into a rig documented (guides/ssh-and-connect); presets (coder, coder-plus-docker) list dev tooling and Docker but no desktop/VNC or browser. Snapshots are reusable base images; their storage price and egress price are not published (null).

Hosted rigs run on third-party sandbox providers (README: "sandbox clouds (E2B, Daytona, Vercel, etc.)"; API `provider` values seen earlier: daytona, e2b, freestyle, vercel); size defaults to that provider's medium tier. Isolation therefore depends on the provider, and the card's single 'vm' isolation and single rate are an abstraction; per-size vCPU/RAM specs (xs/m/l/xl = a0.*, a1.*) are not published.

Plan-gated features (2026-10-14): Team adds Slack/Linear integrations, MCP servers, skills library, GitHub Actions/CI, access rules, org-managed secrets and enforced agent configs; Enterprise adds SSO, SCIM, audit logs, advanced security and network controls, GPUs and custom sandbox sizes, uptime SLA. Own machines/cloud accounts are on every plan (no longer Enterprise-only).
Terms: monthly subscription, auto-charged monthly; 'Limitations are per plan tier, with overage allotments'; price changes need 30 days notice.

Company: Amika (Fixpoint, Inc.), YC Fall 2025, founded 2023, team size 2, New York City (ycombinator.com/companies/amika). Core open source under Apache-2.0 (github.com/gofixpoint/amika); control plane, UI and relay closed source.

fleet.tiers: Free: up to 10 concurrent service-account sandboxes, 3 active users; Team: 10 included then $2/mo per extra concurrent service-account sandbox ($30/active user/month); Enterprise: committed volume pricing.
fleet.notes: Concurrency counts only service-account sandboxes running at once (people-started, paused and stopped ones excluded). Team has no published hard cap, only the $2/slot fee; that is a price, not a capacity reservation for 300/1,000 machines. Account aggregate vCPU/GPU quotas and onboarding verification not published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot captures a configured rig's filesystem as a reusable base image. New rigs that boot from it start with your dependencies, tools, and environment already in place
snapshot_on_demand.note: Filesystem only (no memory). Source rig must be running. CLI `amika snapshot create`, web UI, or `POST /sandbox-snapshots`. Modes: scrub_and_delete (strips injected secrets, deletes source rig) or full (keeps rig running). New rigs boot from it (template); per-repo default snapshot; changelog: snapshots work across repos. Hosted-cloud only, Developer plan and up.

harness_api.quote: Once you have a running rig, you can drive its coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) by sending a single prompt synchronously.
harness_api.note: REST + TS SDK + CLI: `POST /rigs/{id}/agent-send` (blocking), `agent-send-jobs` (async), `POST /agent-sessions/stream` ("Send a message to a coding agent, streaming the reply (SSE)"), `GET /agent-sessions/{id}/events` (SSE), session list/get/patch, resume by session id or --new-session. Harnesses: Claude Code (default), Codex, OpenCode, Pi (architecture doc also lists custom agents via Agent Communication Protocol). Also Slack/Linear/GitHub triggers.

egress_http_rules.quote:
Network Proxy

*Early design. Open-source status TBD.*
egress_http_rules.note: Request-level network authorization/mutation proxy is a roadmap item ("Set authorization rules at the network layer"), not shipped; homepage says "coming soon".

secret_proxy.quote: Secrets are resolved at rig creation time and **copied into the rig VM**, where they are readable as environment variables from inside the rig.
secret_proxy.note: Vault secrets and agent credentials (Claude/Codex OAuth or API key) are injected as env vars/credential files; MCP OAuth tokens are written into ~/.claude/.config.json. Tokenized secrets swapped by a network proxy is a roadmap item ("Secrets Vault ... Early design"); homepage: "Hidden secrets ... (coming soon)".

image_oci.quote: A preset selects the prebuilt environment that boots a rig... Use `coder` for most repositories... `coder-plus-docker`... It does not support the `xs` size tier.
image_oci.note: Rigs boot only from Amika's `coder`/`coder-plus-docker` presets or a snapshot captured from one of those presets; the CLI's `--image` flag for arbitrary Docker/OCI images only applies to ephemeral `amika materialize` containers, not to rig VMs themselves.

anti_bot.quote: Multiplayer cloud workstations for coding agents and humans... provision VMs, load them with your favorite agent(s) and your git repos, and then remote control the agents from any chat surface or app.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (a coding-agent dev workstation, not a browser/stealth-scraping product)

captcha_solving.quote: Multiplayer cloud workstations for coding agents and humans... provision VMs, load them with your favorite agent(s) and your git repos, and then remote control the agents from any chat surface or app.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (a coding-agent dev workstation, not a browser automation/CAPTCHA product)

snapshot_auto.quote: Stop to pause cost ... await amika.stopRig(name); ... Later: resume ... await amika.startRig(name);
snapshot_auto.note: Filesystem/disk state is preserved automatically on `stop` and restored automatically on `start` with no separate snapshot API call needed (persistent_disk). This is disk-only; there is no evidence running-process/memory state is restored (fs snapshot, not mem).

fork.note: A new rig can be created ("forked") from a previously captured filesystem snapshot of another rig via `amika rig create --snapshot <slug>`.

fork_running.quote: A snapshot captures a configured rig's filesystem as a reusable base image. New rigs that boot from it start with your dependencies, tools, and environment already in place
fork_running.note: Forking requires first capturing a filesystem snapshot (an explicit step), then creating a new rig that boots from it as a base image; it is not an instant clone of a still-running machine's live state.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: A snapshot captures a configured rig's filesystem as a reusable base image.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots are filesystem-only (card feature `snapshot: "fs"`); no running-process/memory state is captured or restored when forking.

wake_on_request.note: Stopped rigs must be explicitly resumed via `amika rig start` / `startRig()`; no docs mention a stopped rig auto-waking when an inbound HTTP/SSH request arrives.

volume_attach.quote: Mount persistent file volumes onto rigs and version and control the files. Mount parts of a Filesystem Volume to a rig; when the rig terminates, the files persist.
volume_attach.note: Filesystem Volumes are attachable to rigs (`ro`/`rw`/`rwcopy` mount modes) and persist independently of any single rig.

volume_shared.quote: The CLI's `--delete-volumes` / `--keep-volumes` flags control what happens to associated volumes... When neither flag is set and the rig is the sole reference for a volume, you will be prompted to decide.
volume_shared.note: Volume-deletion logic explicitly references volumes being "referenced by other rigs", implying the same Filesystem Volume can be mounted (at least read-only, per the `ro` mount mode) by more than one rig; concurrent multi-rig read-write mounting is not explicitly confirmed.

live_resize.quote: Create, List, Connect, Delete, Stop, Start, SSH, Code, Agent Send
live_resize.note: The full set of documented `amika rig` subcommands has no resize/resource-update operation; `--size` is only set at `rig create` time, so changing CPU/RAM of a running rig without recreating it is not offered.

own_agent_api.quote: Once you have a running rig, you can drive its coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) by sending a single prompt synchronously.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Amika's first-party API drives YOUR coding harness (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode/Pi) inside the rig; it does not ship its own proprietary browser/computer-use/research task agent.

mcp_server.quote: Give sandboxed agents pre-authenticated access to external tools via MCP servers... Amika stores the OAuth token in the secrets vault, attaches it to each rig... and writes the MCP server configuration into the rig's `~/.claude/.config.json`
mcp_server.note: Amika consumes/wires third-party MCP servers into agents running inside rigs; no evidence of Amika shipping its own MCP server that lets an external MCP client (e.g. Claude Desktop) create/control Amika rigs directly.

lang_python.quote: Base: Ubuntu 24.04; Tools: Git, GitHub CLI, curl, zsh, build essentials, Python, Node.js 24, `npm`, `pnpm`, TypeScript, and `tsx`

lang_node.quote: Base: Ubuntu 24.04; Tools: Git, GitHub CLI, curl, zsh, build essentials, Python, Node.js 24, `npm`, `pnpm`, TypeScript, and `tsx`

public_ipv4.note: SSH and HTTPS access are brokered through Amika's own SSH proxy/host-key pinning and `<rig>.preview.amika.dev` URLs rather than a raw per-machine public IPv4 address; no docs mention an assigned public IPv4 per rig.

ingress_rules.quote: Access rules, org-managed secrets, and enforced agent configs
ingress_rules.note: Team-plan pricing feature (was "Custom network and sandbox access rules"). OpenCode web console access is gated by a provider-managed username/password (docs.amika.dev/guides/opencode); README lists js/service-auth: "deciding who may reach a rig's service: host keys, service tokens and signed links".

guest_firewall.quote: sudo apt-get update ... sudo env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y ...
guest_firewall.note: derived: rigs are full VMs with root/sudo access inside, so nftables/iptables are expected to work; not separately documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: Create Rigs on Kubernetes nodes, sandbox clouds (E2B, Daytona, Vercel, etc.), or (soon) your own computer.
static_egress_ip.note: No pricing/docs page advertises a fixed outbound IP; rigs run across multiple third-party hosted providers, making a stable per-rig egress IP unlikely and undocumented.

windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Rigs boot from Linux (Ubuntu 24.04) presets only; the ARM64/x86_64 support mentioned in docs.amika.dev/install is for the Amika CLI binary's own host platform, not a Windows rig OS.

macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Rigs boot from Linux (Ubuntu 24.04) presets only; macOS support in docs.amika.dev/install refers to the CLI binary's supported host platforms, not a macOS rig.

arm64.quote: Linux | x86_64, arm64 | macOS | x86_64 (Intel), arm64 (Apple Silicon)
arm64.note: That table describes the Amika CLI binary's supported host platforms, not a rig CPU architecture option; no rig size/preset documentation mentions an ARM64 rig tier (sizes referenced are `a0.*`/`a1.*` with unpublished specs).

soc2.note: Enterprise lists SSO, SCIM, audit logs and "Advanced security and network controls" generically; no SOC 2 attestation, badge, or trust page on the pricing, privacy, or docs pages.

hipaa.quote: Enterprise ... Dedicated support, security, and custom infrastructure.
hipaa.note: No HIPAA/BAA mention found on pricing, privacy, or docs pages.

eu_data_residency.quote: your information may be transferred to, stored, and processed by us in our facilities and by those third parties with whom we may share your personal information, in the United States and other countries.
eu_data_residency.note: Privacy policy describes cross-border transfer to the US/other countries by default for EEA/UK/Switzerland residents, with no mention of an EU-region data residency option for rigs.

max_session_h.quote: interface CreateRigRequest { ... autoStopInterval?: number; autoDeleteInterval?: number; ... }
max_session_h.note: No published hard maximum session length; rigs run until you (or your own configured `autoStopInterval` idle timeout) stop them, like a persistent VM — not a fixed platform-imposed cap.

desktop.quote: Any editor that reads your `~/.ssh/config` and supports remote SSH can use the Amika-managed host alias. ... Use a browser: To work with an agent without a local editor, use the OpenCode web console.
desktop.note: Amika rigs are headless Linux dev VMs accessed via SSH or an SSH-backed remote editor / OpenCode web console (a code editor UI, not a GUI desktop). No VNC/remote-desktop/GUI streaming feature is documented anywhere in the docs (checked create-a-rig, presets, ssh-and-connect, opencode, config-toml, roadmap); presets (coder, coder-plus-docker) list dev tooling and Docker only. Product is a coding-agent sandbox, not a virtual desktop, so 'no desktop' is correct.

browser.quote: Rigs can serve OpenCode's web console so you can drive the agent from a browser. Access to that console is protected by a username and password you manage for your organization.
browser.note: The only 'browser' surface documented is a human using their own local browser to reach the OpenCode web console (an agent chat/code UI) or to complete OAuth logins; there is no first-party in-rig browser/browser-automation primitive (no Playwright/Puppeteer/Chrome-for-agents service, no headless browser API) anywhere in the docs, presets, or roadmap. So 'no browser' (in the sandbox-feature sense) is correct.

computer_use.quote: presets (coder, coder-plus-docker) list dev tooling and Docker but no desktop/VNC or browser
computer_use.note: No computer-use / GUI-control capability (mouse/keyboard/screen tool for a desktop or browser) is documented anywhere in llms-full.txt, presets, config.toml reference, or the architecture/roadmap page; the roadmap only lists a network proxy and secrets vault as 'early design'. Product exposes coding-agent harness APIs (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode) over SSH, not a computer-use surface, so 'no computer_use' is correct.

nested_virt.quote: Create Rigs on Kubernetes nodes, sandbox clouds (E2B, Daytona, Vercel, etc.), or (soon) your own computer.
nested_virt.note: derived: no Amika doc mentions /dev/kvm or running VMs/emulators inside a rig. Docker-inside is documented (docker_inside=true) but that only requires a container runtime, not KVM passthrough. Rigs are hosted on third-party providers (Daytona containers, E2B/Vercel Firecracker microVMs) which typically do not expose nested virtualization to the guest, so nested_virt is unlikely to be available and is undocumented either way.

egress_ip_type.quote: Create Rigs on Kubernetes nodes, sandbox clouds (E2B, Daytona, Vercel, etc.), or (soon) your own computer.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: Amika does not publish an explicit egress-IP-type page. Rigs run as VMs/containers on standard cloud infrastructure via Daytona/E2B/Freestyle/Vercel; there is no mention anywhere in docs.amika.dev or the pricing/architecture pages of residential or mobile proxying, so outbound traffic is standard cloud datacenter IP space.

usage_api.quote: OpenAPI spec lists all endpoints: /rigs, /sandboxes, /agent-sessions, etc. No endpoints for /usage, /billing, /metrics, or cost queries per sandbox. Only cost_usd appears in agent session responses (LLM token costs).
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Amika's REST API provides no endpoint to query billable sandbox/rig usage metrics (vCPU-seconds, memory-seconds, storage-seconds, cost). The API returns only LLM token costs in agent-session responses, not infrastructure usage. Pricing is by-resource (vCPU/GiB-hour rates listed on pricing page) but no programmatic query mechanism exists for individual sandbox usage; usage is only available through account dashboards and invoices.

self_host.quote: Unlimited sandboxes on any number of your own machines
self_host.note: On the Free plan and up: "A spare Mac Mini, EC2 in your VPC, or a Kubernetes cluster. Sandboxes there run on every plan and their hours are never charged." amika-hostd runs rigs on your own machine as smolvm VMs (README). Control plane, UI and relay stay closed source and hosted by Amika.

byoc.quote: A spare Mac Mini, EC2 in your VPC, or a Kubernetes cluster. Sandboxes there run on every plan and their hours are never charged.
byoc.note: Bring-your-own cloud accounts/VPC is on every plan (was Enterprise-only); homepage: "Run sandboxes on your AWS, GCP, etc. and spend the credits you already own."

open_source.note: Apache-2.0 core: CLI, amikad (in-VM daemon), sandbox-image, TS SDK. Closed source: amika-control-plane, amika-ui, amika-relay ("What's open source and what's closed source" section). Gateway and sandbox-provisioner "will be open sourced soon".

gpu.note: Hosted GPUs are Enterprise only (no published GPU price, so gpu_types empty); on your own GPU hosts on any plan ("Run GPU evals on GPU hosts").

locations_quote: By default everything runs on the hosted platform at app.amika.dev.
